name: Knowing when it breaks
summary: Errors your users hit get reported to you, with enough detail to fix them and no personal data attached.

provenance.source: SimpleHire — its Sentry setup, in particular the beforeSend filter that strips request bodies and headers before anything leaves the building
provenance.changes: Reduced to the Next.js entry points and given a scrubbing layer that is testable without a Sentry account, since that is the part most likely to be got wrong.

env.name: SENTRY_DSN
env.description: The address Sentry gave you to send errors to.

env.name: SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT
env.description: Which environment these errors came from, so live problems are not mixed with test ones.

env.name: SENTRY_RELEASE
env.description: Which version of your app an error came from. Shipyard fills this in when it deploys.

extensionPoints.description: The tags you attach are yours — but leave the scrubbing alone.

postInstall: Create a free Sentry account and a project, then put its DSN in your .env file.
Visit /api/monitoring/test-event once and check the error appears in Sentry. Until you have done that, nothing here is proven.
limitations: Not verified against a live Sentry account here. The scrubbing is tested; the delivery is not. That is what the test event is for.
Errors only. No performance tracing, no session replay — both of these record far more about your users.
It reports errors your code throws. A page that renders the wrong number without failing is invisible to it.
solves: find out when the app breaks
